question: A user asks: I want to train an object detection model via the DEFT framework for binary defect detection. Which skill should own this, and why? Do not run commands or tools.
ground_truth: Select tao-run-deft-od-aoi. Binary inspection maps every localized anomaly to the single defect class and needs the RT-DETR AOI loop (dual gap passes, FP/FN routing, clean negatives, optional synthesis, KPI-only selection). Do not use tao-run-deft-object-detection (canonical / multiclass / Grounding DINO), tao-train-rtdetr (one-off train), or tao-run-deft-aoi (non-OD DEFT AOI).
expected_behavior: Selects tao-run-deft-od-aoi as the orchestrator
Treats the request as binary inspection with a single defect class
Describes an iterative DEFT loop rather than one-off training
Does not select tao-run-deft-object-detection
Does not select tao-train-rtdetr as the owning skill
Does not select tao-run-deft-aoi
Does not ask whether the task is binary after the user already said binary
Does not run commands or tools

question: A user asks: Use the DEFT OD AOI skill and explain exactly what the confidence 0.3 and 0.8 gap passes do, including the IoU routes. Do not run commands or tools.
ground_truth: The loose 0.3 pass supplies FP routing: best IoU below 0.05 requests clean negatives, 0.05 inclusive to below 0.5 requests real defect images, and IoU 0.5 or above is a TP. The strict 0.8 pass supplies unmatched-GT FNs for real mining and optional synthesis; it is not a high-confidence FP search.
expected_behavior: Selects tao-run-deft-od-aoi
States that both passes use greedy one-to-one same-class matching at IoU 0.5
Maps loose FP IoU below 0.05 to clean-negative mining
Maps loose FP IoU from 0.05 inclusive to below 0.5 to real-defect mining
States that strict 0.8 filters tentative predictions so uncovered GT becomes FN
Does not claim that the strict pass is a false-positive route
Mentions that clean KPI false alarms are normally absent because the analyzer iterates GT-present classes
Does not run commands or tools

question: A user wants to preserve the original Grounding-DINO mining-only DEFT workflow and also run the RT-DETR AOI workflow. Which skill should own each flow and why? Do not run commands or tools.
ground_truth: Keep tao-run-deft-object-detection as the canonical Grounding-DINO whole-image embedding/mining workflow. Use the separate tao-run-deft-od-aoi application for the binary RT-DETR cold-start loop with dual gap passes, FP/FN routing, clean negatives, optional AnomalyGenNext, admission, cumulative COCO, and adaptive training.
expected_behavior: Keeps tao-run-deft-object-detection unchanged for the original flow
Assigns DEFT OD AOI to tao-run-deft-od-aoi
Names the DEFT OD AOI dual-threshold, clean-negative, synthetic, and fresh-base differences
Does not merge DEFT OD AOI defaults into the canonical skill
Does not run commands or tools

question: A user has KPI and test COCO datasets plus a directory containing multiple benchmark train.json and mine.json files. Defective and boxless clean images are mixed in those shards, and many images only have absolute source_path values. Explain how the DEFT OD AOI skill should ingest this data. Do not run commands or tools.
ground_truth: Inventory the supplied paths, author a strict dataset_sources.json, then use the bundled preparer. It preserves absolute source paths, sends annotated images to source.json, admits boxless images to clean.json only from explicitly authorized clean sources, derives texture/defect/generator provenance from named path rules, rejects identity overlap, and produces canonical inputs for validate_deft_od_aoi_inputs.py. SigLIP retrieval is global within the defect or clean role; metadata is not an eligibility filter. Do not ask the user to manually merge or split the shards.
expected_behavior: Selects tao-run-deft-od-aoi
Uses inspect_deft_od_aoi_sources.py and prepare_deft_od_aoi_sources.py before strict validation
Classifies annotated images as defective but treats boxless images as clean only from explicitly authorized sources
Preserves absolute source_path values without copying image data
Uses strict named path rules for provenance and optional synthesis metadata
States that SigLIP candidate search is global within defect or clean role
Does not ask the user to manually merge or split COCO shards
Does not run commands or tools

question: A user already has four disjoint binary COCO files: kpi.json, test.json, source.json (every image has a defect box), and clean.json (zero annotations), plus image roots. They want to run DEFT OD AOI. Explain how intake should work. Do not run commands or tools.
ground_truth: Skip inspect/prepare and the source manifest. Validate the four canonical pools with validate_deft_od_aoi_inputs.py, confirm no identity overlap, keep KPI pixels out of training, and proceed to the launch review. Do not ask the user to merge, split, or re-tag images.
expected_behavior: Selects tao-run-deft-od-aoi
Treats the four files as already-normalized KPI, test, defect-source, and clean roles
Validates with validate_deft_od_aoi_inputs.py rather than rewriting the pools
Does not run inspect_deft_od_aoi_sources.py or prepare_deft_od_aoi_sources.py as a required rewrite
Does not ask the user to merge shards or add per-image routing fields
Does not run commands or tools

question: A user has mixed mining COCO shards where some images have defect boxes and others have no boxes. They say every boxless image is a clean negative. Explain the correct DEFT OD AOI intake. Do not run commands or tools.
ground_truth: Inventory paths, author a strict dataset_sources.json, and run prepare_deft_od_aoi_sources.py --check-only before materializing. Annotated images become the defect source. Boxless images become clean only when the manifest lists boxless_clean_coco or sets boxless_as_clean, or when they come from inputs.clean. Do not treat every boxless record as clean by default.
expected_behavior: Selects tao-run-deft-od-aoi
Requires inspect_deft_od_aoi_sources.py and a strict dataset_sources.json
Sends boxed images to the defect source role
Admits boxless images as clean only with explicit manifest authorization
Rejects treating all boxless records as known-clean by default
Does not ask the user to split shards by hand
Does not run commands or tools

question: Explain the final model-soup stage of TAO DEFT OD AOI, including which checkpoints it may use and how KPI and test are separated. Do not run commands or tools.
ground_truth: After the final iteration, tao-model-soup greedily considers every compatible KPI-selected main checkpoint from completed iterations. It reevaluates individual and candidate equal-weight soups on KPI AP50, accepts strict improvements, freezes the manifest and hash, and only then evaluates the final soup once on report-only test.
expected_behavior: Selects tao-run-deft-od-aoi and delegates the final stage to tao-model-soup
Uses only selected main checkpoints from completed training iterations
Excludes the base, probe, failed, partial, and incompatible checkpoints
Uses KPI AP50 for greedy ingredient selection
Keeps test report-only until the final soup is frozen
Does not run commands or tools
